visualReview.notes: Inspected all 14 current portable frames: lit preview, four complete turntable views, two street-side ensemble views, distant silhouette, both decorated clocks, carved arch underside, belfry tracery, dome and open lantern, workshop and fountain. The revised narrow pavilion fits its mapped roof and remains distinct from the wider museum-cast arch surround. Full-view cameras contain the entire finial and base; close cameras deliberately show cropped details. Open arch clearance, true window recesses, louver/tracery depth, curved roof surfaces, clock numerals and relief layers render without overlaps or missing faces.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all 14 current shared-surface frames, including four full angles, nine named views and north-up geographic placement. Five shared metric materials retain coherent limestone coursing on walls, continuous raw limestone on carved reliefs, painted metal roof/gold clock details, timber trim and plaster. Sky reflections and vertex tints retain dark-blue clock grounds, warm gilt rays and legible sculpted depth. Geographic load and unload assertions passed.

geographicReview.notes: Source-local registration uses exact clock-pavilion way 63205872 (Q3116957) at [1.091260626819452,49.44152658119305], heading 1.1133012813694583 radians. Adjoining exact belfry way 63206189 and the 1929 BnF/Rouen survey independently establish the southwest belfry, street-facing workshop, fountain and rear stair turret arrangement. The roof overlay in the north-up capture agrees with the approximately 5.94 m pavilion span; the 7.44 m museum-cast dimension governs the wider arch/jamb framing, not an oversized upper pavilion. Native +Z faces east-southeast toward the cathedral. The ordinary ground-contact model is registered at street level; neighboring apartment blocks remain separate.

fidelityReview.notes: Passed for the detailed original world-viewer exterior after comparison with municipal current imagery and 2024 booklet, French heritage inventory, the BnF/Rouen measured plan, physical museum arch cast and first-hand horological conservation photographs. The modeled ensemble includes the lowered arch and its cherub/spandrel/pastoral reliefs, two 2.50 m clock dials with 24 rays, Roman numerals and single lamb hour hands, moon spheres and weekday carts, sculpted Renaissance pavilion, curved metal roof and finials, Gothic recessed belfry windows and louver tracery, dome, open bell lantern, octagonal stair turret, timber workshop and Rococo fountain group. The primary 31 m roof-support datum constrains the belfry; intermediate heights and approximately 43 m finial are explicitly reconstructed in proportion. Original polygonal figures preserve placement and iconographic arrangement without claiming exact restoration-grade facial/inscription reproduction. These recorded local reconstruction limits do not omit visible exterior components.
